author_or_org: Raphael Shu, Nilaksh Das, Michelle Yuan, Monica Sunkara, Yi Zhang

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The report identifies designing collaboration protocols and evaluating system effectiveness as significant challenges, especially for enterprise applications.
claims.quote: However, designing the collaboration protocols and evaluating the effectiveness of these systems remains a significant challenge, especially for enterprise applications.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The report evaluates two operational modes: coordination for complex task completion via parallel communication and payload referencing, and routing for efficient message forwarding between agents.
claims.quote: We evaluate two key operational modes: (1) a coordination mode enabling complex task completion through parallel communication and payload referencing, and (2) a routing mode for efficient message forwarding between agents.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The benchmark uses handcrafted scenarios from three enterprise domains that are publicly released with the report.
claims.quote: We benchmark on a set of handcrafted scenarios from three enterprise domains, which are publicly released with the report.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Inter-agent communication and payload referencing mechanisms achieved 90% end-to-end goal success rates in coordination capabilities.
claims.quote: For coordination capabilities, we demonstrate the effectiveness of inter-agent communication and payload referencing mechanisms, achieving end-to-end goal success rates of 90%.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Multi-agent collaboration improved goal success rates by up to 70% versus single-agent approaches, payload referencing improved code-intensive task performance by 23%, and a routing mechanism can substantially reduce latency by selectively bypassing agent orchestration.
claims.quote: Our analysis yields several key findings: multi-agent collaboration enhances goal success rates by up to 70% compared to single-agent approaches in our benchmarks; payload referencing improves performance on code-intensive tasks by 23%; latency can be substantially reduced with a routing mechanism that selectively bypasses agent orchestration.
